lines.speaker: Agamemnon
lines.text: [sighs] So you went mad, Ajax. You killed yourself, and you fully intended to massacre the rest of us too. Fine. But why do you blame Odysseus? When he came down here the other day to consult the prophet, you wouldn't even look at him. You didn't even deign to speak to a comrade in arms. You just took these massive, haughty strides and marched right past him.

lines.speaker: Ajax
lines.text: With good reason, Agamemnon! He was the sole cause of my madness. He was the only one who stood against me for the armor.

lines.speaker: Agamemnon
lines.text: What, did you expect to go totally unchallenged? To win without a fight?

lines.speaker: Ajax
lines.text: In *this* case, yes! The armor was family property. It belonged to my cousin. The rest of you—all vastly superior men—declined the contest and yielded to me. But the son of Laertes? A man I saved countless times when the Phrygians were about to hack him to pieces? *He* demanded to be considered the better man, and more worthy to carry those arms!

lines.speaker: Agamemnon
lines.text: In that case, my noble friend, you should blame Thetis. She ought to have simply handed the inheritance over to you as the next of kin. Instead, she brought the armor out and put it up for public competition.

lines.speaker: Ajax
lines.text: No. I blame Odysseus. He was the only one who stepped up to claim it.

lines.speaker: Agamemnon
lines.text: You have to forgive him, Ajax. He was only human. He was reaching for glory—the sweetest prize there is, and the exact same reason every single one of us risked our lives. Besides, he defeated you fairly, and with a jury of Trojans, no less.

lines.speaker: Ajax
lines.text: I know perfectly well *who* condemned me. [pause] But we aren't allowed to speak ill of the gods. As for Odysseus... I could never stop hating him, Agamemnon. No, not even if Athena herself ordered me to.
